Details: The Academy — a GED-focused academic RPG wrapped in a retro CRT desktop metaphor. Players pick starter perks/traits, then study, take assignments, and progress through a simulated 1980s-style institutional operating system.
Three user-facing artifacts: a React web app (retro CRT desktop OS), an Express API server, and an offline-first Expo mobile companion for Android/iOS.

pnpm multi-artifact workspace. Packages live under artifacts/* (runnable apps), lib/* (shared libraries), and scripts/. Dependency versions are centralized via the pnpm catalog in pnpm-workspace.yaml.
MIT — see the LICENSE file at the repository root.
Node.js 24 or newer.
pnpm 10+. A preinstall hook rejects npm/yarn — always use pnpm.
A PostgreSQL database is required by the API server. Connection string is provided via DATABASE_URL.
DATABASE_URL (Postgres), SESSION_SECRET (sessions), and OpenAI credentials for the AI description engine (proxied in the Replit environment).
Run a single install at the repository root; pnpm links all workspace packages.
Push the Drizzle schema to your database (development only). Use push-force to bypass interactive prompts.
React 19 + Vite 7 + wouter routing + Radix UI + Tailwind CSS 4. Mounted at base path /. UI entry flow: src/App.tsx -> RetroBootScreen -> NeoCrtDesktopShell.
Express 5 backend served at /api. Routes are declared with absolute /api/... paths in src/routes/routes.ts and wired via registerRoutes(app) in src/app.ts. Built with esbuild to a CJS bundle.

Expo + expo-router companion app. Offline-first: a deterministic on-device engine powers all gameplay with no connection; the live API only enriches responses when reachable. Each response is tagged online/offline.
@workspace/game-engine is the single source of truth for offline content, GED templates, and world layout shared by web and mobile.
@workspace/db exposes the Drizzle ORM schema. schema.ts is the source of truth for the server.
lib/api-spec holds the OpenAPI spec (openapi.yaml). Orval generates React Query hooks (lib/api-client-react) and Zod schemas (lib/api-zod) from it.

Game modules (schema, perks, stats, curriculum, contentPack) are copied into the web frontend at src/shared/ (imported via the @shared/* alias) rather than shared through a lib, to preserve the legacy import structure.

Server-side OpenAI endpoint (gpt-5-mini) enhances text-adventure flavor in two modes: Location mode (atmospheric flavor text) and Examine mode (contextual object descriptions). Results are cached client-side.
Starts the Express backend on port 5000 (dev script builds then starts with source maps).
Starts the Vite dev server for the web frontend.
Starts the Expo/Metro dev server for the mobile companion.
Typechecks shared libs (tsc --build) then every artifact and scripts package.
Full typecheck plus builds for all packages.
Regenerate React Query hooks and Zod schemas after editing the OpenAPI spec.
Apply Drizzle schema changes to the development database.
The mobile artifact has a vitest test suite covering the offline engine.

The web frontend uses its own fetch layer (src/lib/queryClient.ts) with same-origin relative /api/... requests and credentials: include. OpenAPI codegen is intentionally NOT used for the legacy web frontend.
Tailwind CSS 4 (@tailwindcss/vite), Radix UI primitives, class-variance-authority, framer-motion, lucide-react icons.
lib/api.ts is a smart fetch layer: every helper tries the live API first, then falls back to the deterministic offline engine. Responses carry a source tag (online | offline).
Deterministic offline content generation lives in lib/gameFallbacks.ts and the shared @workspace/game-engine library.
Retro CRT theme: Space Mono font (@expo-google-fonts/space-mono), phosphor-green palette in constants/colors.ts, consumed via the useColors hook.
metro.config.js is monorepo-aware (watchFolders + nodeModulesPaths include the workspace root) — required for EAS cloud builds to resolve hoisted deps. Do not revert to the single-package default.
EAS build config is in eas.json. The preview profile produces an installable .apk; production produces a Play Store app bundle. Requires an Expo account; run from the mobile artifact directory.

The API address is baked in at build time via EXPO_PUBLIC_DOMAIN in eas.json (currently empty, so APKs are offline-only). Set it to the published domain to enable live AI enrichment and content-pack sync.
Routes are split into routes.ts (game/API routes), health.ts, and index.ts. Middleware, AI helpers, NLP, procedural generation, and storage each have their own directory under src/.
express-rate-limit, cookie-parser, CORS, and bcryptjs are wired in the API server.
Zod (zod/v4) with drizzle-zod for schema-derived validators; @workspace/api-zod carries the OpenAPI-generated Zod schemas.
All workspace packages use the @workspace/* scope and are private.
Shared dependency versions (react, vite, drizzle-orm, zod, tailwind, etc.) are pinned in the pnpm catalog — add new shared deps there, reference them with "catalog:".

TypeScript ~5.9, strict project references for libs (tsconfig.base.json / tsconfig.json at root). Legacy web frontend has intentional pre-existing strict-TS errors; Vite/esbuild transpile despite them.
Run apps via their workflows, never a root-level pnpm dev/build.
artifacts/academy/src/shared/schema.ts duplicates lib/db/src/schema/schema.ts. If shared DB types change, update BOTH copies in sync.

The web app was ported from a legacy codebase (.migration-backup/) with behavior/visual parity as the goal. Pre-existing bugs and strict-TS compliance are intentionally out of scope — avoid drive-by refactors.
The mobile artifact intentionally calls the API via direct fetch. Do NOT add DB or OpenAPI codegen to the mobile package.
npm and yarn are blocked by a preinstall hook; lockfiles other than pnpm-lock.yaml are deleted automatically.
Production build: pnpm run build. The API server bundles to dist/index.mjs (esbuild, CJS) and serves the app; the web frontend builds via vite build.
Distribute via EAS builds (APK / app bundle) or Expo Go for quick device testing during development.
